children: Tether, issuer of the world’s largest dollar-pegged stablecoin USDT, could face insolvency risk if declines in gold and Bitcoin prices continue, according to an analysis.

On Nov. 21, digital-asset analyst PoziDiablo wrote on X, formerly Twitter, citing Tether’s third-quarter reserve report that the company’s reserves could fall below its liabilities if prices of non-cash assets such as gold and Bitcoin keep sliding.
As of Sept. 30, Tether had total assets of $191.45 billion and total liabilities of $183.5 billion. Its excess reserves, or assets minus liabilities, stood at about $7.95 billion.

PoziDiablo identified Tether’s non-cash holdings, which account for 27% of its assets, as a key risk factor. He said those holdings total about $52 billion, including $19.1 billion in gold, $8.4 billion in Bitcoin, $4.2 billion in equities and $14.2 billion in secured loans.

He added that recent price declines may already have wiped out a substantial portion of those excess reserves. Bitcoin has fallen more than 30% and gold about 15%, he wrote. If the value of other assets, including secured loans, also drops 15% to 20%, Tether could move close to insolvency.

title: Tether Faces Insolvency Risk if Gold, Bitcoin Price Declines Persist
